mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening labor market conditions, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 55% of months with positive PAYEMS growth, or the monthly PAYEMS growth rate shows no significant correlation with 5-day SPX returns (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 3.5% for three consecutive months, it signals a tightening monetary policy cycle that reduces liquidity and increases discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of triggered instances, or the FEDFUNDS rate threshold fails to predict returns with a Rank IC > 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and rise in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a robust labor market, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through improved consumer confidence and corporate profit margins.
failure_condition: The joint movement of UNRATE and PAYEMS fails to predict 60-day SPX returns (Rank IC < 0.03) or the interaction effect is not significant (p-value > 0.05) in a regression of SPX returns on the interaction term.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a decline in housing starts (HOUST) combined with a slowdown in industrial production (INDPRO) signals an impending economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of late-cycle expansion periods when HOUST and INDPRO both decline, or the interaction between HOUST and INDPRO fails to predict returns (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly increase in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates expanding economic activity, which supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of quarters with positive GDPC1 growth, or the quarterly GDPC1 growth rate shows no significant correlation with 20-day SPX returns (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation rate exceeds 2.5% for two consecutive months, it signals persistent inflationary pressures that prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten policy, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of triggered instances, or the CPIAUCSL threshold fails to predict returns with a Rank IC > 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates a broad-based economic slowdown, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through reduced business investment and consumer activity.
failure_condition: The joint decline in INDPRO and HOUST fails to predict 5-day SPX returns (Rank IC < 0.03) or the interaction effect is not significant (p-value > 0.05) in a regression.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% signals labor market weakness and economic deceleration, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of late-cycle expansion periods when UNRATE exceeds 4.5%, or the UNRATE threshold fails to predict returns (Rank IC < 0.05).
